subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs before they can run on inherited model defaults?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes operator consent, shipped cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the security boundary.

options.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow inherited-model warning
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block only when a recurring agentTurn job inherits a high-cost default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split into existing guardrail trackers
options.body: Resolve provenance, reason-aware retry, and gateway budget enforcement in their separate issues while accepting that this combined consent/model/cost report remains an integration risk.

recommendation.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across plugin scheduled-turns and the product/security boundary visible in related reviews and commits.
